strengths: The paper presents an intuitive diagnostic—conditional entropy over semantic partitions—and clearly motivates its connection to class commitment and time-localized diffusion control.
The Gaussian-mixture analysis provides useful intuition for the VP speciation scale t_s = (1/2)log d and contrasts it with the broader transition under VE/EDM dynamics.
Experiments cover both class-conditional EDM2-XS/ImageNet and text-conditioned Stable Diffusion 1.5. The appendix reports samplers, NFE, noise schedules, sample counts, and guidance-quality metrics.

The limitations section appropriately acknowledges posterior-calibration error, bias from using the unconditional distribution as a class-complement proxy, prompt entanglement, and Stable Diffusion 1.5 failures.
weaknesses: Soundness: central equations are inconsistent. Equation 8 gives a negative entropy derivative, whereas Appendix Equation 18 correctly derives a nonnegative derivative. Appendix Equation 22 then drops the g_t^2/2 factor. Algorithm 1 accumulates gamma log gamma terms without the required minus sign, apparently producing negative entropy. These discrepancies directly affect the paper's principal quantity.

The claimed phase-transition result is not established rigorously. The appendix shows pointwise limiting behavior away from u=1 and then infers a spike from endpoint entropy values; it does not prove concentration, transition width, or convergence of the entropy rate, and leaves important assumptions about class count and mean geometry implicit.

The practical estimator is not adequately specified. Essential posterior updates are deferred to another paper, while Algorithm 1 has ambiguous sample indexing and normalization. Moreover, replacing the complement with the unconditional distribution and imposing a balanced prior changes the estimand. The statement that conditional entropy becomes equivalent to Jensen-Shannon divergence is incorrect: for a balanced mixture it equals log 2 minus the Jensen-Shannon divergence.

The guidance analysis further changes the quantity into a cross-entropy, as the appendix acknowledges. A cross-entropy along guided trajectories need not retain the monotonicity or information-production interpretation used throughout the main text, so the conclusions about guidance redistributing semantic information are insufficiently justified.

The empirical evidence does not establish the repeated claim that the method reliably localizes semantic emergence. ImageNet and text-to-image results rely mainly on visual inspection of selected denoised trajectories; there are no ground-truth emergence annotations, quantitative correlations, competing diagnostics, uncertainty estimates, or controlled interventions based on the detected windows.

Stable Diffusion prompts were manually selected after checking adherence, creating selection bias. The manuscript reports only a small number of prompt families and admits cases where prompt differences are entangled or the target attribute is absent, but it does not quantify failure rates or robustness.

Reproducibility is incomplete despite useful high-level settings: no code is provided, and posterior-update formulas, derivative/smoothing procedures, grid-search ranges, seeds, complete prompt sets, and estimator sensitivity analyses are missing.

Originality and significance are presently limited. Conditional entropy/mutual information are standard, the online posterior tracker is adopted from prior work, and the Gaussian-mixture time scale follows rather directly from an SNR calculation. No downstream improvement from entropy-selected guidance or scheduling is demonstrated.

Presentation is generally readable, but numerous notation errors, typographical issues, and contradictions between the main text, appendix, and pseudocode make the technical claims difficult to verify. The impact statement is also boilerplate and does not discuss dataset bias or risks inherited from ImageNet, LAION-5B, and text-to-image generation.

strengths: The paper presents a coherent and intuitively useful perspective: conditional label entropy offers a time-resolved view of semantic commitment, while binary semantic partitions can probe distinctions at different abstraction levels.

The Gaussian-mixture setup makes the proposed quantity analytically tractable and connects it to Fisher divergence, posterior log-ratios, signal-to-noise ratio, and the logarithmic VP speciation scale.

The empirical scope is broader than a purely theoretical treatment: experiments cover both ImageNet-conditioned EDM2-XS and text-conditioned Stable Diffusion 1.5, include guidance interventions, and report several generation-quality metrics and sample counts.

The manuscript is generally well organized and visually clear. Its limitations section candidly acknowledges posterior-calibration error, bias from the unconditional complement proxy, prompt confounding, and weak prompt adherence. I found no major new ethical concern beyond the familiar risks associated with pretrained image generators and their training data.
weaknesses: Soundness: the central entropy-rate equations are internally inconsistent. Equation (8) gives a negative Fisher-divergence rate, whereas Appendix Eq. (18) derives a positive rate for the same forward-time conditional entropy; Appendix Eq. (22) then drops the g_t^2/2 factor. Algorithm 1 also accumulates gamma log gamma+(1-gamma)log(1-gamma) without the required minus sign, apparently producing negative entropy. These are not harmless presentation details because entropy production is the paper's principal diagnostic.

The asymptotic argument is not sufficiently rigorous. Appendix A infers a spike largely from vanishing behavior on either side and endpoint entropy values, without establishing the limiting profile or its concentration. It also incorrectly says the standard deviation of Lambda is of the same order as its mean when the stated scalings are d^((1-u)/2) and d^(1-u), respectively. Assumptions needed for the multi-component and hierarchical interpretation are not developed.

The trained-model estimator is not adequately validated. Its key posterior update is left as an undefined operation and delegated to Algorithm 2 of another paper. There is no comparison against a setting with known posteriors, a held-out classifier, forward-noised labeled data, or another calibrated estimator, so it is unclear whether peaks measure semantic commitment or accumulated denoiser/calibration error.

The ImageNet computation changes the target quantity materially: it imposes a balanced binary prior and replaces p(x|Z != i) with p(x). The resulting quantity is related to, but not literally equivalent to, Jensen-Shannon divergence as claimed. No ablation quantifies the bias from either choice, despite conclusions being drawn at the class level.

The central empirical claim that entropy 'reliably localizes' feature emergence is supported mainly by visual correspondence in a few selected trajectories. There are no annotations, detector-based emergence times, correlations, hypothesis tests, uncertainty estimates, or systematic failure rates. Stable Diffusion prompts were manually selected after checking adherence, creating substantial selection bias, and the appendix itself reports failures when prompts are not followed or variants alter more than the intended attribute.

The guidance results are primarily descriptive and do not demonstrate practical utility of the proposed diagnostic. Guidance intervals are optimized directly using FID or FDDINOv2 rather than selected from entropy profiles, and the benefit of limited guidance was already established by cited prior work. Thus the experiments show post-hoc association, not that entropy enables better control or scheduling.

Originality and significance are limited in their current form. Conditional entropy/mutual information is a natural diagnostic, the posterior-tracking mechanism is borrowed, and the Gaussian-mixture calculation largely recovers a known speciation scale. Semantic partitioning is potentially useful, but the paper does not establish a quantitatively reliable method or a new downstream capability.

Reproducibility is inadequate: no code or repository is provided, the posterior-update formula is absent, and grid-search ranges, resolutions, seeds, numerical differentiation/smoothing choices, prompt lists, class aggregation details, and variability across runs are missing. The manuscript contains enough model and sampler settings to indicate the intended setup but not enough to independently reproduce its main curves.

Presentation requires technical cleanup beyond ordinary typos: forward versus reverse time and the sign of 'entropy production' are not consistently defined, several equations or algorithmic statements conflict, and strong mechanistic language such as 'semantic decision making' is used where the evidence only establishes changes in an estimated distribution-overlap statistic. The impact statement is also perfunctory and does not discuss inherited dataset or image-generation risks.

strengths: The paper offers an intuitive diagnostic—conditional entropy over semantic partitions—for locating when particular distinctions become resolved during diffusion. The ability to select partitions makes the framework more informative than a single global uncertainty measure.

The Gaussian-mixture analysis usefully connects this diagnostic to the established VP speciation scale, obtaining the expected t_s = (1/2) log d + O(1) behavior and contrasting it with the broader transition under VE/EDM parameterizations.

Experiments span both class-conditional EDM2-XS/ImageNet and text-conditioned Stable Diffusion 1.5. The guidance study is potentially useful: it suggests that different guidance intervals redistribute semantic commitment differently, while the prompt-pair examples illustrate decisions at different spatial or spectral scales.

Presentation is generally clear, figures are legible, and the appendix reports models, schedules, NFE, sample counts, guidance intervals, and evaluation metrics. The limitations section candidly discusses posterior calibration, the class-complement approximation, prompt adherence, and attribute confounding; these admissions should not themselves be penalized.

The work has moderate originality and practical significance: neither conditional entropy nor the posterior-tracking estimator is new, but relating partitioned entropy to speciation and using it to study time-localized guidance is a useful synthesis. No unresolved material ethical concern is apparent for this diagnostic study.
weaknesses: The central empirical claim that entropy “reliably” localizes semantic emergence is supported mainly through visual correspondence. There is no independent annotation or feature detector, quantitative correlation between entropy transitions and attribute appearance, comparison against alternative diagnostics, hypothesis test, or uncertainty analysis. The Stable Diffusion study uses only a few manually selected prompts and explicitly states that prompts were chosen after checking adherence, creating substantial selection bias.

Several mathematical inconsistencies weaken soundness. Equation (8) gives a negative entropy derivative, whereas forward noising should increase H[Z|X_t] and Appendix Equation (18) derives the positive sign. Algorithm 1 likewise accumulates gamma log gamma terms without the required minus sign and initializes entropy to 1 despite otherwise using natural logarithms. Appendix B also writes the likelihood ratio with the same distribution in numerator and denominator. These may be typographical, but they make the defined quantity and implementation ambiguous.

The phase-transition argument is more heuristic than the wording suggests. In Appendix A.2, the text incorrectly says the fluctuation scale is of the same order as the mean for u<1; it is the square root of that order. The existence of a spike at u=1 is then inferred from endpoint behavior rather than established through a controlled limit for the entropy derivative. Assumptions concerning the number and geometry of mixture components are also not explored.

The trained-model estimator is not adequately validated. ImageNet class complements are replaced by the unconditional distribution and priors are reset to 1/2, so the reported quantity is an approximate equal-weight Jensen–Shannon overlap rather than the originally defined class conditional entropy. Under guidance, the paper states that it becomes a cross-entropy evaluated under a changed trajectory distribution. Consequently, guided and unguided curves do not transparently measure the same information-theoretic object, making claims about “information redistribution” stronger than the evidence warrants.

Reproducibility is incomplete: the manuscript provides no code, exact local posterior-update equations, differentiation or smoothing procedure, random seeds, grid-search ranges, full prompt list, or Monte Carlo confidence intervals. “Visual convergence” at 200–300 samples is not a quantitative convergence assessment. The expensive claim of 50,000 samples for every grid setting is also difficult to interpret without the grid itself.

The guidance experiments optimize intervals using FID or FDDINOv2 and then interpret their overlap with entropy profiles, but they do not demonstrate that entropy-derived intervals predict effective guidance schedules on held-out classes or prompts. Such an intervention would be the strongest evidence for the claimed practical basis for time-localized control.

Overall, the idea is promising and the paper is readable, but central reliability and operational-control claims need stronger quantitative evidence, and the definition/sign/estimator inconsistencies should be resolved before others can confidently build on the result. These issues outweigh the merits in the current version.

strengths: Soundness: The exact entropy-production identity relating dH(Z|X_t)/dt to posterior competition and pairwise score gaps is clearly derived, and the isotropic Gaussian-mixture analysis identifies a coherent control parameter governing both quantities.

Originality: Connecting conditional-entropy dynamics to statistical-physics notions of class speciation is conceptually interesting. Partitioned entropy is a useful extension that can probe particular semantic distinctions rather than aggregating all classes.
Significance: The diagnostic could be valuable for studying when semantic choices arise and for designing time-localized guidance, if its empirical validity is established more rigorously.

Evaluation covers both a controlled setting and trained generators: VP/VE Gaussian mixtures, ImageNet EDM2-XS, Stable Diffusion 1.5, and an additional SDXL example. The estimator-bias decomposition and convergence experiments are particularly useful.

Presentation is generally clear and well organized. The appendices provide derivations, sampling settings, sample counts, compute requirements, guidance-search results, and candid examples of estimator and prompt-adherence failures.

The paper explicitly acknowledges calibration error, complement-model bias, imperfect prompt adherence, and unintended prompt-induced distribution shifts. No major incremental ethical risk is apparent beyond the usual concerns associated with pretrained image generators.
weaknesses: Soundness: The extension from Gaussian mixtures to general class structure is substantially less rigorous than claimed. The argument establishes asymptotic suppression before and after the proposed window, but the conclusion that a non-negligible peak must occur at t_rs+O(1) relies on informal assertions about score gaps and continuity; it does not prove the peak's existence, uniqueness, or localization under stated assumptions.

The trained-model experiments do not independently validate that an entropy peak marks semantic commitment. The main evidence consists of a few selected denoised trajectories and qualitative coarse-to-fine interpretations. There are no external attribute detectors, controlled ground-truth emergence times, quantitative correlations, or comparisons against simpler diagnostics such as conditional-score distance or denoiser-output differences.

The practical observable differs materially from the theoretical one: priors are forced to 0.5 and the true class complement is replaced by the unconditional model. Although synthetic bias studies suggest that transition timing can survive in the tested mixtures, this does not establish validity for learned, misspecified models or text-prompt distributions. The paper itself shows that rebalancing changes profile shape.

The guidance analysis is especially difficult to interpret. Appendix B states that evaluation on guided trajectories produces a cross-entropy, not the conditional entropy analyzed theoretically. Consequently, differences in Figure 3 need not represent a redistribution of semantic information, yet the main text repeatedly gives them that interpretation without a corresponding theorem or calibration experiment.

Significance is not fully demonstrated: the method is presented as a basis for time-localized control, but no intervention is selected from the estimated entropy profiles and shown to improve generation. Guidance intervals are instead optimized directly using FID or FDDINOv2, making the entropy analysis retrospective rather than operational.

The Stable Diffusion evidence is small and potentially selection-biased. It uses a few manually chosen prompt families, and the authors manually verify prompt adherence. Additional examples repeat the same qualitative pattern, but no systematic prompt suite, uncertainty analysis, or predefined evaluation protocol is provided.

Reproducibility is only partial. Important details such as the exact posterior-update implementation, smoothing bandwidth used before differentiation, interpolation choices, complete guidance grid, all prompts, and random seeds are missing, and no code or artifact availability statement is given. Entropy-production curves can be sensitive to precisely these choices.

Presentation is polished, but terminology occasionally overstates the evidence: phrases such as 'reliably localizes,' 'quantitative view,' and 'principled basis for control' are stronger than the predominantly qualitative validation supports. The distinction among true conditional entropy, balanced-prior Jensen-Shannon separability, and guided cross-entropy should be prominent throughout rather than confined largely to the appendix.

The impact statement is perfunctory. While the work has limited direct ethical risk, a more appropriate discussion would briefly address dependence on LAION/ImageNet-trained generators, inherited representation biases, and the possibility that semantic timing conclusions reflect dataset or model biases.

strengths: Soundness: The exact entropy-production identity and the isotropic Gaussian-mixture analysis are technically motivated and expose a useful interaction between posterior competition and pairwise score separation. The VP-versus-VE scaling comparison is particularly informative.

Originality and significance: Connecting conditional-entropy dynamics to the statistical-physics notion of class speciation is an interesting synthesis. Partitioned entropy could become a useful semantic diagnostic if validated more rigorously.

Presentation: The paper is generally well organized, with clear figures, extensive derivations, estimator-bias studies, convergence checks, computational-cost reporting, and an unusually substantive limitations discussion.

Experimental scope: The authors examine both class-conditional and text-conditional models, include guidance experiments, and add SDXL results and explicit failure cases rather than hiding unfavorable behavior.
Ethics: The work itself presents limited direct risk, and I found no unresolved material ethical concern affecting the technical recommendation.
weaknesses: Soundness: The claimed extension to “general class structure” is not established at the stated level of generality. The argument analyzes leading first- and second-moment differences and then reasons heuristically that the entropy-production peak must lie in the speciation window. Vanishing contributions before and sufficiently after that window do not prove a peak at the claimed time, and classes distinguished only through higher-order structure are not treated despite the broad claim.

Soundness: The practical observable differs materially from the theoretical quantity. The experiments rebalance the natural class priors, replace the class complement with the unconditional model, use learned rather than exact likelihood increments, smooth the estimated entropy before differentiation, and—in the guidance study—measure a cross-entropy under guided trajectories. Synthetic bias checks are helpful but do not establish that peak locations remain faithful in trained models under all these approximations.

Evidence and significance: The central claim that the diagnostic “reliably localizes” semantic formation is supported mostly by qualitative alignment with selected denoised predictions. On ImageNet, only a few highlighted classes receive visual interpretation; no labeled feature-emergence times or independent quantitative ground truth are used. In the text-to-image setting, the evidence comprises a small, manually selected prompt set without error bars, systematic controls, or statistical evaluation.

Evidence and originality: There are no meaningful comparisons against simpler or existing diagnostics, such as classifier confidence, conditional–unconditional score distance, SNR-based schedules, representation-space probes, or previously proposed critical-window measures. Consequently, the experiments do not show that entropy adds information beyond quantities already computed by the estimator.

The Stable Diffusion interpretation is substantially confounded. A base prompt and an augmented prompt define two entire conditional distributions rather than a clean partition of one semantic variable. Their entropy can reflect prompt adherence, composition, layout, or other unintended changes rather than the targeted attribute. The manuscript acknowledges this limitation, but the current qualitative experiments do not resolve it.

The guidance analysis is descriptive rather than causal or actionable. Guidance intervals are optimized using external quality metrics and only afterward related to entropy profiles; the entropy diagnostic is not used prospectively to choose an interval, and no held-out experiment shows that entropy-selected control improves quality. Thus the claimed “principled basis for time-localized control” is not demonstrated.

Reproducibility is incomplete: no code or artifact link is provided; Algorithm 1 leaves key sampling and posterior-update operations undefined; the Gaussian smoothing bandwidth is omitted; the guidance grid and selection protocol are not specified; and uncertainty or seed variation is absent from the principal results. These omissions matter because peak locations depend directly on numerical integration, smoothing, and model calibration.

Presentation and ethics: The prose and visual presentation are polished, but some conclusions are stronger than the displayed evidence. The impact statement is boilerplate and does not discuss inherited dataset or generative-model biases, although these are secondary concerns given the diagnostic nature of the contribution. Overall, the promising framing does not compensate for the gap between the exact theory, the altered practical estimator, and the largely qualitative validation.

strengths: Soundness: The exact entropy-production identity cleanly connects posterior class competition with pairwise score separation, and the isotropic Gaussian-mixture analysis convincingly recovers the VP speciation scale while clarifying the different VE/EDM scaling behavior.

Originality and significance: Interpreting class-conditional entropy as an operational signature of speciation is a useful bridge between statistical-physics accounts of diffusion and diagnostics applicable to trained models. Partitioned entropy is a sensible extension for probing individual semantic decisions.

Empirical breadth: The paper examines synthetic mixtures, ImageNet-512 with EDM2-XS, and prompt-level distinctions with Stable Diffusion 1.5 and SDXL. The convergence and estimator-bias studies in Figures 7–8 are particularly valuable.

Presentation: The manuscript is well organized, visually polished, and unusually transparent about estimator bias, prompt-adherence failures, and the limitations of using an unconditional model as a complement proxy.

Reproducibility and ethics: The appendix reports models, samplers, schedules, NFEs, sample counts, metric settings, guidance intervals, hardware, and runtimes. The work poses no substantial direct ethical risk, and the limitations discussion is appropriately candid.
weaknesses: Soundness: The extension from Gaussian mixtures to general class structure does not fully prove the headline claim that the entropy-production peak coincides with speciation. Showing that contributions vanish before and sufficiently after speciation establishes localization only heuristically; it does not supply a lower bound, uniqueness result, or rigorous peak-location guarantee in the critical window.

The strongest empirical claim—that the diagnostic reliably identifies when particular semantics emerge—is supported mainly by visual agreement with selected denoised trajectories. There is no quantitative ground truth, attribute detector, human evaluation, peak-localization metric, or comparison against simpler diagnostics such as prediction differences, score distances, or classifier confidence.

The guidance analysis has an important interpretational caveat: Appendix B states that evaluating the posterior quantity under guided trajectories produces a cross-entropy rather than the conditional entropy defined by the theory. Consequently, Figure 3 does not by itself establish a redistribution of semantic information in the strict information-theoretic sense, and the discrepancy is not quantified.

The practical observable differs materially from the theoretical quantity through balanced artificial priors, unconditional-complement substitution, posterior approximation, numerical differentiation, and smoothing. The synthetic bias studies are helpful but do not validate the combined approximation on realistic data, and Figure 8 shows that prior balancing can alter profile shape.

The text-to-image evaluation covers few prompt families and uses manually verified prompts, creating selection bias. The paper itself shows that prompt non-adherence and unintended distribution shifts can make the entropy profile track more than the intended attribute, limiting the current evidence for generality.

Reproducibility is adequate but incomplete: no code or artifact release is identified, the posterior-update implementation is largely deferred to prior work, and important details such as smoothing bandwidth, complete prompt lists, grid-search ranges, profile normalization, and uncertainty on reported peak locations are missing. Dataset biases inherited from ImageNet and LAION are also not discussed.
